clue.text: The means I contrived to control the sail

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the rope that does this job

indicators.note: contrived means artfully put together, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor explains that the device they rigged up is how they work the sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' shuffles the letters of THE MEANS I; the definition describes the rope by its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the rope or line by which a yacht's mainsail is trimmed and controlled.

clue.text: She includes me inter alia

indicators.note: includes means one word holds the other within it, here the Latin word around the little word

parts.note: taken as written, the second word of the Latin phrase
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a woman counts herself among the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' is the container signal; 'inter', Latin for among, merely completes the familiar phrase 'inter alia', meaning among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as 'she'.

clue.text: They tend to hurry up before the ship rounds the point

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for hurry is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to hurry is to run

indicators.note: rounds means the ship's letters go around the point

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Sailors in a hurry wait for their ship to round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses in a down clue and 'rounds' is the container; 'before' only says which piece comes first. 'Tend' looks like a verb of tendency, but it means care for.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital staff who care for the sick are the people who tend patients.

clue.text: He's taking in any mistreated animals

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man takes in stray animals that have been badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' is the anagram signal; 'taking in' looks like a container but is only a link, since the letters must all be shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are scavenging carnivores of Africa and Asia, a kind of wild beast.

clue.text: Is she French?

parts.note: the three words also ask to put 'is she' into French, where they read ..., which run together form a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Estelle is a girl's name of French origin, so it names a 'she'.

clue.text: Like mistletoe? Patricia's to go out for it

indicators.note: to go out suggests the letters going out of their places, so the name is rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S, read as Patricia is

explanation.surface: Patricia is told she must go out and fetch the mistletoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go out' rearranges PATRICIAS; the S counts because 'Patricia's' means 'Patricia is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe grows on host trees and draws nourishment from them, living as a parasite.

clue.text: It could be in a modest part of Kent

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something might be found in an unassuming corner of an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges IN A MODEST; KENT is a county in south-east England, and this is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is the county town of Kent, so it forms part of that county.

clue.text: Observes and steals money

definitions.meaning: pays attention to, as in heeding something
read literally: helps oneself to a banknote

explanation.surface: Someone watches carefully and pockets cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pays heed; read literally it means helping oneself to a banknote, which is theft.

clue.text: Food taken from the hand

parts.note: sounds like feeding from the palm, but a bunch of this fruit is called a hand, and one is picked off it

explanation.surface: Someone eats something out of a person's palm.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunch of these fruits is called a hand, each fruit a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow fruit grows in clusters called hands, from which single fruits are broken off.

clue.text: She gets the theatre in an uproar

indicators.note: an uproar is a state of turmoil, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman causes a commotion in the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an uproar' rearranges THEATRE plus IN; 'gets the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrietta is a woman's name, so it can stand for any 'she'.

clue.text: Club porter

parts.note: looks like a doorman at a gentlemen's club, but means someone who carries golf clubs

explanation.surface: A doorman at a private members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course this assistant carries the player's bag of clubs.

clue.text: Schedule means item is thrown out by the board

indicators.note: thrown out means scattered from its proper order, so the four letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A planning document says an agenda point was rejected by the directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges ITEM into TIME; 'means' and 'by' only link it to TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a programme listing when events happen, like a train schedule.

clue.text: Replace points in a car engine

definitions.note: describes the part by where it is found

indicators.note: replace means put back in a different place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A mechanic is told to fit new contact points in a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace' rearranges POINTS; car ignition points were a part needing regular replacement, which is the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This sliding cylinder moves inside each cylinder of a motor and drives the crankshaft.

clue.text: Space given for the rest of the teachers

definitions.text: Space given for the rest of the teachers

parts.words: Space given for the rest of the teachers
parts.note: reads as room left for the remaining teachers, but means a room where teachers take their rest

explanation.surface: Room is found for the remaining members of the school faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: In a school, this lounge is where the teaching body relax between lessons.

clue.text: Fling it up, wildly cheering

indicators.note: wildly means in a disorderly way, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd tosses something into the air while cheering madly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges FLING IT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uplifting raises the spirits, just as cheering news does.

clue.text: Show fight having provision for spectators

parts.note: with means having, as in a house with a garden
a stand is a structure for spectators at a sports ground

explanation.surface: A sports ground with seating puts on a boxing bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist or hold out against an attack is to put up a fight.

clue.text: Revised directions

definitions.meaning: brought up to date, as in a fresh edition
three compass points, north, east and west, taken together

explanation.surface: Instructions that have been updated.
explanation.definitionFit: A revised version is fresh; and the letters are the compass points north, east and west.

clue.text: Catch a number up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the number word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone tries to catch a number going upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TEN backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a fish is to catch it, and figuratively to win or gain.

clue.text: A question of motive

parts.note: reads as a matter concerning motive, but means the one-word query that asks for a reason

explanation.surface: It all comes down to the reasons behind an act.
explanation.definitionFit: This word asks for reasons, so it is the interrogative used to ask about motives.

clue.text: Joint league champions?

definitions.meaning: a cut of meat for roasting, here beef from the upper leg

explanation.surface: Two teams share the title.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPSIDE is a lean cut of beef; split as TOP SIDE it is the best team in a league.
explanation.definitionFit: This lean beef roasting cut is a joint; read as two words it is the leading team in a league.

clue.text: Lock-keeper comes out of the rain

indicators.note: comes out of suggests these letters emerge rearranged from the words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A canal official comes in out of a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out of' rearranges THE RAIN. 'Lock-keeper' suggests a canal official; a lock here is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine mesh holds hair in place, keeping locks of hair tidy.

clue.text: Essay which won't be pointless

definitions.meaning: an attempt, the old sense of essay
in rugby a touchdown scores points, so it is never without points

explanation.surface: A piece of writing that will have a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Essay here is an attempt, not a composition; in rugby union a try scores five points.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an essay; in rugby the touchdown called this always earns points.

clue.text: In its ascent, the sun is like a ball

definitions.text: In its ascent, the sun is like a ball

parts.words: In its ascent, the sun is like a ball
parts.note: a sunrise could be put as rise, Sol, which run together suggest the name of a fried ball of minced meat

explanation.surface: A rising sun looks round like a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol is the Latin name for the sun; the clue plays on the sound of 'rise, Sol'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small ball or cake of minced meat coated in breadcrumbs and fried.

clue.text: They involve a shift in one's beliefs

indicators.note: involve here means wrap up together, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Converting means changing what you believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involve' rearranges A SHIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious creeds or convictions are a person's faiths.

clue.text: Agreement for one side on first of October

parts.note: right is one side, the other being left

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: Two parties agree on one side's terms on the first of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' takes O from October.
explanation.definitionFit: This British colloquial word is an exclamation of assent, like 'OK'.

clue.text: They're for firing ovens, perhaps

definitions.meaning: places where guns are fired at targets
cooking stoves, of which an oven is an example

explanation.surface: Kilns are used for firing pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' suggests a kiln for pottery, but means shooting at a rifle range.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting grounds are rifle places; kitchen stoves with ovens are also called by this name.

clue.text: One way to loaf is to walk leisurely

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A guide to idling suggests taking an unhurried walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' seems to mean idle about, but supplies a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble or saunter is to walk at an easy pace.

clue.text: They strive to organise partisans

indicators.note: to organise is to put into order, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Activists work hard to marshal a band of guerrillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to organise' rearranges PARTISANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopefuls who aim for success are people striving towards a goal.

clue.text: Go round with a list at half-term

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

indicators.note: half picks the first two of the four letters of term

explanation.surface: A school timetable sets out what happens at the mid-point of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TE from term; 'half-term' is a British school holiday in mid-term.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn or spin about an axis is to go round.

clue.text: Showing a profit-a reward for virtue?

definitions.meaning: what goes to virtuous people, read literally

explanation.surface: Being in profit is the prize for behaving well.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in profit; read literally, a reward goes to virtuous people.

clue.text: Admitting being the proprietor?

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper confesses to being the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up is admitting a fault; possessing a property makes one its proprietor.

clue.text: Fish or fruit only

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A diner chooses between seafood and a fruit-only option.
explanation.definitionFit: This flatfish is a European food species related to the Dover variety.
